issues.description: Method parameter mismatch for Lecture.addGuestStudents: the problem statement UML and the solution implementation declare addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) with a single int parameter, but the template Lecture class declares addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) with an extra boolean parameter. This inconsistency will cause students to be unsure which signature to implement and can lead to compilation or test failures if tests expect the single-parameter version.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the problem statement and solution by changing the template method signature to: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { ... } and remove the boolean parameter. If input validation is intended to be part of the exercise, instead update the problem statement/UML and the solution to document and implement the two-parameter signature consistently (including the boolean's semantics and how tests will exercise it).

issues.description: The exercise specifies a method to add guest students as addGuestStudents(int) (problem statement and UML). The template Lecture class declares a method public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) (extra boolean parameter), while the solution implements public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents). This mismatch in the method parameter list (an extra boolean in the template) means students cannot directly implement or call the method as described in the task and UML, causing confusion about the required signature and expected usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template method signature with the problem statement and solution by changing the template declaration to: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) and implement any input validation internally (do not require an extra boolean parameter). This makes the required behavior and usage match the UML, tests, and solution.
